title: Split an ID range into batches, up to the last int

blocks.text: The search reindexer walks a range of record IDs in batches. A tenant whose IDs were allocated from the top of the `int` range, up to `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, has to be reindexed too, and so does a range whose size isn't a multiple of the batch size.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/IdBatches.java`: `forEachBatch(...)` hands the range `firstId` to `lastId`, both included, to the handler in batches of at most `size` IDs, in order.
When you're done, every ID of the range is handed over exactly once, whatever `int` the range ends at, and the method returns once the last batch is handed over. About four lines in total.

cases.says: an ordinary range is handed over in order, in batches of the given size
a range that ends at Integer.MAX_VALUE is handed over once, its last batch ends at that ID, and the walk stops there
when one ID is left over after the full batches, it is handed over as a batch of its own

origin.section: A Loop Ends Only When Its Condition Turns False, and int Overflow Can Keep It True

concepts: With < instead of <= on an inclusive bound, a last batch of a single element is never processed.
A loop whose int counter must pass Integer.MAX_VALUE, or whose step overflows, never makes its condition false; a long counter ends it.
